Honest caveat up front: these are dark, low-contrast images, and limbs overlap the black torso, so some of this is best-effort inference, not certainty.

**1) Left/rear arm (Images 1 & 2)**
- In Image 2 (guard): the rear arm starts at the shoulder (roughly at the head's lower edge / top of the torso), extends back-down, elbow bent pointing backward/down, and the forearm folds forward-in toward the body. A faint dark rounded shape behind the torso (Image 2, ~waist height, slightly left of the body) reads as the rear upper arm/shoulder mass; the forearm is largely hidden against the torso.
- In Image 1 (idle): the rear arm is essentially invisible — the dark silhouette swallows it. I cannot confidently trace elbow direction there.

**2) Right/front (sword) arm**
- Image 2: starts at the shoulder just below head height, upper arm angles down-forward, elbow bends, forearm angles forward-down toward the glowing sword grip (the bright cyan handle near mid-torso height). Roughly an L-shape, elbow pointing down/back.
- Image 1 (sheathed): the arm folds sharply back toward the hip so the hand meets the sheathed katana's grip; elbow appears bent and tucked. The exact elbow point is obscured.

**3) Neck:** No distinct neck segment is visible in either image — the head circle sits essentially directly on/overlapping the torso top. If a neck exists, it's hidden inside the silhouette.

**4) Arm origin:** The arms start at/below the head — shoulder level is at the very bottom edge of the head circle, not at the head's center height. The head noticeably overlaps the shoulder region.

**5) Anatomical impossibilities:** Nothing clearly impossible at this resolution. The limb bends (elbow folding directions) look plausible for a stick figure. The main issues are stylization, not impossibility: no visible neck, the head-to-shoulder overlap, and in Image 2 the rear arm is so occluded that a full joint chain can't be verified. I also can't confirm hands/fingers — the figure has none visible, which is standard stick-figure style rather than an error.

What I genuinely can't see: the rear forearm's endpoint in both images, any elbow in Image 1, and whether there are two separate arms vs. one rendered arm in the idle pose.
